$comment: Gemfall beat 3 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 3A). Every ending sets exactly one member of `crossing`: rest_dry_end sets crossed_dry on entry; scene_swept sets river_took_us on entry and is the only door to rest_wet_end and rest_setback. The two never share a path - scene_swept is reached only from a missed crossing activity or failed crossing check or a lost drake fight, and rest_dry_end only from a completed crossing activity or passed crossing check. The setback needs a swept party to fail a crawler check AND lose the crawler fight. The expansion's episodes (kettle camp, wagon, river view, passes, Dilly, gem toll, camp vote, night rope, wake fee, east landing, mouth shore) set only chapter-local flags.
title: The Long Mile

plate.narration: At Stone Crossing, a mossy troll rests one enormous palm on the first stone. A bird is building a nest on his shoulder. The line can wait. Every traveler owes him a story or a riddle.

objectives.label: Put the centaurs' road markers back
Got a fair rate from the river drake

goal.text: Pay the toll at Stone Crossing and get across the river.

steps.label: Camp in the line for the night

facet_drakes_rate.name: The Drake's Rate
facet_drakes_rate.text: The newest piece on a river drake's hoard shelf. Marked PAID, underlined twice.

ossley_reed_knot.name: Ossley's Reed Knot
ossley_reed_knot.text: A reed knot from Old Ossley. "Later. When I'm going your way." It never dries.

scene_east_road.narration: Marda's rumor board said the crossing line was moving again. Your job tonight: pay the troll's toll at Stone Crossing and get across the Great River. First comes the Long Mile. Its markers are gone, and someone is cooking porridge on MILE 3.

check_markers.prompt: Put the mile markers back in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Mile one, mile two, mile three, all the way to the river. A centaur gallops up, counts them twice, and looks like she might cry with relief.

onFailure.narration: Every marker goes back in. MILE 7 goes back in between MILE 2 and MILE 3, so the road now runs backwards for a bit. A centaur thunders past, groans, and fixes it without stopping. No guide for you today.

scene_courtesy.narration: You wave first, from far off, tail curled politely away. A centaur on the ridge waves back so hard her sash ribbons tangle.

scene_fennick.narration: Fennick Longstride, a road-warden centaur, checks her stitched map-sash. "At the crossing, take the upstream edge. The stones are only half under." Then she trots off to fix her signs.

scene_queue.narration: At Stone Crossing, giant flat stones cross the river. The line fills the road. A woman sells soup up and down it. Near the front, six brass hats are sneakily moving the line's rope.

check_rivals.prompt: Find the fresh brass-hat knots in the rope that marks the line

onSuccess.narration: You point out that the rope has fresh knots, the knots are brass-hat knots, and one of them still has a brass hat caught in it.

onFailure.narration: The Brassbuckles smile, tip their six matching hats, and are somehow forty places ahead of you. Nobody saw anything. Everybody saw everything.

scene_rivals_caught.narration: A troll sends the Brassbuckle Expedition and its six matching hats to the back. They leave behind their secret shortcut: a rope tied across the shallows.

scene_troll.narration: The toll troll, Old Lintel, rests a mossy palm on the first stone. "A story," he rumbles. "Or a riddle." Every traveler owes one. A bird is building a nest on his shoulder.

scene_troll_riddle_account.narration: You bring the prides' riddle score, the way manticores always have. Old Lintel's total is different. It always is. He hands you a smooth luckstone "for keeping the argument going."

scene_troll_ask_riddle.narration: Ask your riddle out loud. Old Lintel tries answers like stones in a wall. Then he asks one so old nobody knows its last word. He takes your guess anyway.

scene_troll_tell_story.narration: Old Lintel hears every word of your story. The bird finishes its nest. At last he rumbles, "Good. That one's paid."

scene_troll_hum.narration: Old Lintel stops listening to the line. He listens to the bridge. "The stones are humming," he rumbles. "Every pack here hums one note, older than this bridge." So there is one more toll: "Where did you get that? And where is it going?"

scene_troll_hum_show_ember.narration: You hold out the Ember Facet. Old Lintel lays one finger beside it on the bridge. The bridge hums back, deep in your boots. "Hear that?" he says. "Older than me."

scene_troll_hum_dont_know.narration: "We don't know yet," you say. Old Lintel nods, which takes a while. "Then that's the toll," he says. "Find out."

scene_troll_hum_answer_honest.narration: You tell him about the red stone that landed by your boot at the Exchange, and where you think the stones are going. "Good," says Old Lintel. "Keep asking it."

rest_queue_camp.narration: The travelers camp for the night. Toffee is shared, then stolen by a goat. Under the bridge, something rubs numbers off a slate and writes bigger ones.

scene_drake_shelf.narration: Under the bridge, the river drake lies on a rock shelf like a cat on a windowsill. Beside it sits one new gem that hums, and a slate that says RATES. The drake keeps writing bigger numbers.

check_drake.prompt: Haggle with a river drake who has done this before

onSuccess.narration: You offer a song, a shiny button, and a really excellent fish story. The drake weighs all three, decides it has been treated like a professional, and nudges the humming gem across the shelf.

onFailure.narration: The drake listens to your offer, then raises its rates. Then it raises them again, just to watch your face. The humming gem stays exactly where it is.

scene_drake_deal.narration: The new gem is warm. It hums in your palm like a purring cat. The drake writes PAID on its slate and underlines it twice.

encounter_drake.narration: The drake does not blink after all. Its sister pops up. She handles complaints.

onVictory.narration: Splashed and outplayed, the drakes huddle. "Fair," huffs the big one. "You won the rate."

onDefeat.narration: A tail as long as a canoe sweeps you, quite politely, into the current.

scene_crossing_bank.narration: Your turn at last. Brown water hides the last stepping stones. Wait for a lull, use a line you prepared, or risk a scramble. A frog in a flat boat watches from the reeds.

scene_ossley_price.narration: That is Old Ossley. He ferries people when the stones are under, never for coin. His price: the song you hum when nobody listens, a proud memory, and a promise to carry something for somebody, someday.

check_crossing.prompt: Step from drowned stone to drowned stone across the last stretch

onSuccess.narration: Slip, wobble, step, step, step. The river grabs at your ankles, grumbles, and lets go. You stand on the east bank with boots that are, astonishingly, dry, in the middle of a traffic jam.

onFailure.narration: One stone is not where it was yesterday. The river decides it wants you more than the bank does, and everybody goes in together with a splash that startles a heron into next week.

check_crossing_easy.prompt: Hold on tight through the last fast stretch

onSuccess.narration: The current tugs, and sulks, and lets you go. Your boots touch the east bank and they are, astonishingly, dry.

onFailure.narration: Right at the fastest bit, a drake's wake rolls by, and the river decides it wants you more than the bank does. Everybody goes in together with a splash that startles a heron into next week.

rest_dry_end.narration: The east bank! The Eastern Plains roll away, gold and green. On the far ridge, a manticore waves first. Wave back. Tonight you camp dry, with that old note humming in your packs.

variants.text: A centaur helped you fix the road markers.
The night rope still has the troll's muddy thumbprint.
The frog ferryman helped you across.

scene_swept.narration: The river carries you south like a parcel nobody signed for. Past the line, past the Sunward banks, on and on. The heron follows, just to disapprove.

scene_mouth.narration: At last the river lets you go on the eastern shore. Far off, haze hangs over the Bone Yard. A frog in a very old hat fishes you out. "Old Ossley," he says. "Later. When I'm going your way." He hands you a reed knot. It stays wet.

scene_crawlers.narration: The beach is covered in bone chips laid in neat spirals. Then a spiral stands up. Bone crawlers! Little scuttlers in borrowed fossil shells. They clatter straight for your humming packs.

check_crawlers.prompt: Fool a bone crawler swarm with something that glitters

onSuccess.narration: You fling a wet, glinting spoon down the beach. Every crawler turns at once and pours after it like a rattling carpet. Somewhere behind you, you hear them start arranging it in a spiral.

onFailure.narration: The spoon glitters. Your packs hum. The crawlers are not stupid. They clatter around the spoon and keep coming.

check_crawlers_leave.prompt: Stomp off the beach looking as big as you possibly can

onSuccess.narration: Arms up, elbows out, stomping like giants. The crawlers decide you are far too large to bother with and scuttle back to their spirals, muttering.

onFailure.narration: Somebody stomps into a rock pool, sits down very suddenly, and is no longer the biggest thing on the beach. The crawlers notice.

encounter_crawlers.narration: The crawlers clatter through the reeds toward whatever hums.

onVictory.narration: Bopped and outrun, the crawlers clatter off in a huff to fix their spirals.

onDefeat.narration: There are far more crawlers than it looked. They swarm the packs like a rattling blanket.

rest_wet_end.narration: You build a driftwood fire on the eastern shore and steam like dumplings. You will walk into the Eastern Plains the wet way, from the south. Old Ossley's boat is gone. His reed knot is still damp.

variants.text: A centaur helped you fix the road markers.
The night rope still has the troll's muddy thumbprint.
The frog ferryman helped you across.

rest_setback.narration: The crawlers carry off the snacks, two bootlaces and the map. Chasing your boots takes all day. Old Ossley poles past and nods once, as if to say: you'll still get there. Just later.

scene_kettle_camp.narration: A camp is boiling its kettle on painted firewood: THIS WAY AROUND. NOT THAT WAY. GO UPSTREAM, PLEASE. Those are the centaurs' detour signs! The campers think they are very colorful logs.

scene_kettle_camp_swap_kindling.narration: You trade your kindling for the signs. The campers think that is a great deal. You walk on with an armful of arrows pointing every which way.

check_kettle.prompt: Tell the campers which sinkhole each painted sign steers wagons around, before the kettle whistles

onSuccess.narration: You explain that the signs steer wagons around the new sinkholes and away from the river's fast bits. The campers go pink, stand every sign back up by the road, and pour you tea to say sorry. It is excellent tea.

onFailure.narration: The campers nod, and nod, and say "oh, absolutely," and then set the kettle back down on NOT THAT WAY. You leave them arguing about which way that way is.

scene_stuck_wagon.narration: A wagon is stuck axle-deep in a rut. Its driver folds his arms. "Admiring the view," he says. The view is mud. Push hard, or unload his humming crates first.

check_wagon.prompt: Everybody heave a loaded wagon out of a rut

onSuccess.narration: One, two, HEAVE! The wagon pops out of the rut like a cork from a bottle. The driver says he was just about to do that himself, and gives you a honeycake for your trouble anyway.

onFailure.narration: One, two, HEAVE! Nothing. Again! Nothing. The mule sighs, leans into its harness, and pulls the whole wagon out by itself, looking at you as if you were luggage.

scene_stuck_wagon_unload.narration: You lift down the humming crates. "Gems for the north," says the driver. The lighter wagon rolls free. "Still admiring the view," he adds.

scene_river_view.narration: Stone Crossing stretches into brown water. A gray heron fishes from a half-drowned stone. Under the bridge flicks the tail of a river drake, a small river dragon with big opinions about money. On the slope, a centaur hunts for her signs.

check_heron.prompt: Learn the crossing by watching a heron fish it

onSuccess.narration: Left foot, right foot, never the middle. The heron only ever steps on the upstream edge of the stones, where they are only half under. You learn its line by heart. The heron notices you learning it and looks deeply offended.

onFailure.narration: The heron catches you staring. It stares back. It is much better at staring than you are, and by the time you blink it has flown off with a fish, and you have learned nothing at all except humility.

scene_river_view_queue_map.narration: A boy with a tray sells you a map of the line for one button. It is a long wiggly sausage with YOU ARE HERE at the very end. That turns out to be true.

scene_river_view_give_signs.narration: It's Fennick Longstride, the road-warden centaur. She hugs her signs like lost puppies. On the last one she scratches an arrow to the upstream edge of the crossing. "For you," she says.

scene_skip_passes.narration: The six brass hats call themselves the Brassbuckle Expedition. One strolls down the line selling SKIP PASSES. "Skip the line!" she sings. At the front, the toll troll, Old Lintel, takes stories, not passes.

check_small_print.prompt: Read the tiny writing on a SKIP-A-STORY pass

onSuccess.narration: You squint. In letters the size of ants it says: VALID ON DAYS WHEN THE RIVER RUNS UPHILL. You read it out loud. The whole line laughs, and the Brassbuckle sells exactly no passes at all. She tips her hat to you, quite sportingly.

onFailure.narration: The print is so small it might just be ants. One of the letters walks away. You hand the pass back politely, and the Brassbuckle moves on down the line, selling briskly.

scene_skip_passes_no_thanks.narration: "Stories are the toll," you say. Nearby families put their purses away. The Brassbuckle turns her tray around. Now it says COLLECTIBLE PASSES.

scene_first_story.narration: A girl named Dilly is practicing her first troll story. "I have the start," she whispers, "but no ending." Help her find one, or give her your best story and make up another.

scene_first_story_help_ending.narration: Everyone suggests an ending. Dragon? Wedding? Sandwich? Dilly picks the sandwich and practices until she stops whispering.

scene_first_story_give_story.narration: You tell Dilly your best story. She runs off to practice it. Now you need something new for Old Lintel. Behind you, Dilly roars your best line.

scene_troll_new_story.narration: You make up a story on the spot. It wobbles. It has a goat in it for no reason. "Never been told before," says Old Lintel. "Rare, that." On the far stones, Dilly waves.

scene_gem_toll.narration: A prospector slaps a humming gem on the bridge. "Paid!" Old Lintel does not move. Explain the story toll, or lift the gem and see what the bridge does.

scene_gem_toll_explain.narration: "A story or a riddle," you whisper. The prospector goes red. "I wanted a gem. I got a gem. The end." Old Lintel thinks. "Paid," he says.

scene_gem_toll_lift_gem.narration: You lift the gem. The bridge stops humming. Set it down, and the note comes back. Old Lintel rests his huge palm beside it.

choice_camp_spot.narration: Pick one spot to camp. The goat family has a honeycake, good for trading with the drake. Next to the brass hats, you can stop their rope trick. By the water, you can learn a slower crossing.

choice_camp_spot_by_goat.narration: The goat eats a map and most of a hat. Its family says sorry with a honeycake. Save it for the drake. Keep it away from the goat.

choice_camp_spot_by_brass.narration: Beside the Brassbuckles, you hear whispers and a rope being coiled. If they sneak out tonight, you can sit on their rope.

choice_camp_spot_by_water.narration: You watch the current: fast in the middle, slower at the upstream edge. Now you know the longer lull for tomorrow. Your socks have learned the river too.

scene_night_rope.narration: A midnight splash! The Brassbuckles are sneaking across with a rope, and the black river tugs at the first one. Brace the rope together, or wake the troll.

check_night_rope.prompt: Everybody grab the Brassbuckles' rope before the river does

onSuccess.narration: You grab the rope just as the river grabs the first Brassbuckle. Everybody pulls. Out he pops, soaked, minus his hat, and says thank you so quietly you nearly miss it. All six creep back to their places in the line and stay there.

onFailure.narration: The rope zips through your hands, but the Brassbuckles grab it too, and everybody ends up in one dripping heap on the bank. One brass hat sails off downstream, spinning. Nobody says anything. Everybody goes back to bed.

scene_night_rope_wake_troll.narration: You shake Old Lintel's arm. Trolls wake up the way mountains do: slowly. By the time one eye opens, the Brassbuckles have crept back to bed. "Good," he rumbles.

scene_night_rope_sit_on_rope.narration: You roll over and sit on their rope. They tug. You sit. They tug harder. You yawn. At last they give up. You sleep well, on a very lumpy rope.

scene_wake_fee.narration: Morning. The drake has put up a sign: WAKE FEE: ONE GOOD JOKE. An unpaid drake might splash your crossing for fun. Risk a joke, pay a fish, or use a trade you earned.

onSuccess.narration: "What do you call a fish with no eyes? A fsh." A long silence. Then the water bubbles and bubbles: the drake is laughing so hard it has to come up for air. It taps the slate with its tail. PAID.

onFailure.narration: You tell your best joke. The drake looks at you. You explain the joke. The drake looks at you harder. Then it writes NOTED on the slate, which is somehow worse than not laughing, and sinks out of sight.

scene_wake_fee_pay_fish.narration: You fish a fish out of the travelers' soup. The drake takes it with great dignity and writes PAID. The soup seller counts her pot and decides not to ask.

scene_wake_fee_show_paid.narration: You hold up the Drake's Rate, PAID underlined twice. The drake knows its own handwriting. It wipes the slate and writes, very neatly: FRIENDS AND FAMILY RATE.

scene_east_landing.narration: On the east bank, a donkey named Parsnip is blocking the carts. Her driver says she hates humming gem crates. Parsnip lies down with her eyes shut, to make this clear.

scene_east_landing_move_crates.narration: You move the humming crates to the last cart. Parsnip gets up and leads the line. "Such a fuss," says the driver, sneaking her an apple.

scene_east_landing_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get them? Where are they going?" The driver looks at his crates. "Off the rush. North, to whoever pays." Parsnip snorts.

scene_swept_float.narration: Everybody floats on their back, arms and legs out, like a row of starfish. The river carries you more gently. The heron disapproves of starfish too.

scene_mouth_shore.narration: You wring out your socks. A stranger's hat washes up at your feet. All along the tide line, chips of old bone lie in neat spirals. Hundreds of them.

check_spirals.prompt: Trace each bone-chip spiral with a finger and find what it curls around

onSuccess.narration: The spirals are not random. Each one curls around a bare patch where something humming must have lain, and every chip leans away from it, like grass in a wind. Even the beach flinches from the stones. Your packs hum. Somewhere up the beach, something rattles.

onFailure.narration: You count spirals until you lose count, and start again, and lose count again. The heron watches you do it three times, cannot bear it, and flies off. Somewhere up the beach, something rattles.

scene_mouth_shore_dry_dance.narration: Hop, shake, flap, hop. It is not a real dance, but it mostly works. Up the beach, the bone chips begin to rattle.

interaction_planks.narration: With the wagon free, you and the driver lay planks across the rut. The next cart rolls over without a bump. "Plank money," says the driver gruffly, and hands you a few coins.

interaction_hats.narration: Another brass hat sets up a game on a barrel: three cups, one shiny button. "Find it and win a prize!" she calls. Her hands begin to fly.

interaction.cue: Watch the glow, then choose the cup with the button.

onSuccess.narration: There is the button! The line cheers. The Brassbuckle pays up with a little brass whistle.

onFailure.narration: Wrong cup. Under it sits a very small spider, who looks offended.

onAssisted.narration: The Brassbuckle slows down until the whole line can follow. You find the button. She pays up with a little brass whistle.

interaction_hum.narration: Old Lintel hums his low note until it settles in your ears. "Remember that," he says. "Songs travel farther than lines." You hum it back, and the bridge hums with you.

interaction_pot.narration: The camp's cook waves you over to her huge supper pot. Together you tip porridge into the waiting bowls, and she wraps a hot supper for you. Down the road, a wagon is stuck.

scene_crab_dusk.narration: At sunset the river goes click. Glassback crabs climb the bank, their glass shells glowing. They think the humming packs mean dinner! "Somebody do something!" cries the soup seller.

encounter_crabs.narration: The crabs click and clatter up the bank. Turn them around before they reach the carts.

scene_crabs_turned.narration: The crabs grumble back into the water, as if they only came to look. The soup seller hands you a warm bottle. "Waiting tonic," she says. "On the house."

scene_crabs_sent_home.narration: The crabs keep coming. Click, click, click. Then Old Lintel slaps one huge hand on the bridge. THUD. The crabs take one look and scuttle home. No tonic tonight.

scene_wake_fee_pay_coin.narration: You drop a coin on the rock. The drake bites it, because it bites everything. It writes PAID, and underneath, smaller, PROMPT SERVICE.

interaction_markers.narration: Three posts have lost their numbers. One shows a kettle, one a wagon rut, one the crossing. Use the clues to put them in order. The kettle post smells like breakfast.

interaction.cue: Share the clues. Put the places in road order, nearest first.
clues: The kettle camp comes before the wagon rut.
The crossing comes after the wagon rut.
Start at this end of the road, not the river.

onSuccess.narration: Kettle, rut, crossing. A road-warden centaur sees the straight posts and trots over to help.

onFailure.narration: The crossing post goes first. A passing centaur fixes it, but can't stay to guide you.

onAssisted.narration: A passing centaur helps you check the clues. Then she stays to show you her shallow line.

interaction_heron.narration: The heron steps from stone to stone between the reeds. Follow its glow to its last fishing spot. Do not try a staring contest. The heron always wins.

interaction.cue: Follow the glow, then choose the heron's last position.

onSuccess.narration: You mark its last perch: the upstream edge. The heron leaves with a fish.

onFailure.narration: You mark an empty patch of reeds. The heron is gone.

onAssisted.narration: A traveler points out the glow. Together you mark the upstream edge, a checked line, with help.

interaction_night_rope.narration: A brass hat bobs in the black water, then its owner. Keep the bank end of the rope steady while the Brassbuckles climb out. Pull together, not just harder.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the rope marker is in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: Out comes the soaked scout, then his hat. He lends you the rope for the morning.

onFailure.narration: The Brassbuckles land in a dripping heap. Everyone is safe, but their rope washes away.

onAssisted.narration: Old Lintel pins the rope with one huge finger while you pull. The Brassbuckles lend you the rope, muddy thumbprint and all.

interaction_crossing.narration: The brown current runs hard, then softens. Without a prepared line, the lull is short. Watch the marker, then step. The heron is supervising.

interaction.cue: Step when the marker is inside the gold lull.

onSuccess.narration: You step in the lull and reach the east bank dry. The heron complains anyway.

onFailure.narration: You step into the hard current. Off the stones you go, toward the southern shore.

onAssisted.narration: The frog in the boat calls the lull for you. You land dry.

interaction_crossing_prepared.narration: The brown current runs hard, then softens. Your prepared line marks the slower edge, so you have longer to step. The heron is supervising.

interaction.cue: Step when the marker is inside the gold lull.

onSuccess.narration: You step in the lull and reach the east bank dry. The heron complains anyway.

onFailure.narration: A wake catches your step. The river carries you off toward the southern shore.

onAssisted.narration: The frog in the boat calls the lull for you. You land dry.

interaction_ferry.narration: You give your song, a proud memory and a promise. Old Ossley nods. Keep the load level while he poles through the fast water. His hat does not wobble.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the ferry load.

onSuccess.narration: The boat slips into the eastern reeds. Dry boots, and a promise still to keep.

onFailure.narration: A wake tips the low boat. The current sweeps everyone south.

onAssisted.narration: Old Ossley steadies the load with his pole. The boat reaches the east bank dry.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, playful, a little spooky but never scary; a river crossing that is a real hazard and a busy, funny line

npcVoices.fennick: Fennick Longstride, a road-warden centaur; brisk, proud of her stitched route-sash, deeply offended that people burn road markers for firewood
npcVoices.old_lintel: a stone troll toll-taker, mostly moss; speaks very slowly, hears everything in full, palm always on the bridge; asks only 'where did you get that, and where is it going?'
npcVoices.drake: a river drake; semi-sapient, transactional, writes its rates on a slate; communicates in huffs, tail-taps and underlinings
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, six people in matching brass hats; smooth, smiling, always somehow ahead in the line
npcVoices.old_ossley: frogfolk ferryman; very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation; answers the question you meant; never asks for coin
npcVoices.kettle_campers: a rush camp boiling a kettle on the centaurs' detour signs; cheerful, agreeable, say 'oh, absolutely' and do not change
npcVoices.wagon_driver: a big rush wagon driver in a bigger coat, stuck in a rut, too proud to ask for help; 'admiring the view'
npcVoices.dilly: a small girl from a carpet caravan telling a troll her first ever story; nervous, then magnificent
npcVoices.prospector: a pushy prospector who tries to pay the troll toll with a gem; tells the shortest story ever told
npcVoices.parsnip_driver: a caravan driver landing on the east bank, arguing with his donkey Parsnip, secretly very fond of her

interaction_pot.narration: You have barely gone three steps when behind you something goes HISSSS. The camp's supper pot, a copper pot as big as a barrel, is boiling over, and the cook is waving her ladle like a flag. "Tip it off the fire before it scorches!" she cries. "One to tip, and everybody else to hold the pole!" There is porridge in there for the whole camp.

interaction.cue: Friends hold the pole steady while someone tips the pot.

onSuccess.narration: The pot tips slow and steady, and the porridge pours out in one fat brown ribbon into a row of waiting bowls. Not a drop in the fire. The cook mops her forehead with her sleeve and wraps a hot supper in a cloth for you. "Better than the porridge at MILE 3," she says. "That is not hard." Down the road, a wagon is stuck right across the way.

onFailure.narration: The pole wobbles, and the pot tips too soon. Porridge slides down the side in one slow slop and lands in the fire. Hiss. The cook looks at it for a while. "Crunchy," she says bravely. "We call it crunchy." Down the road, a wagon is stuck right across the way.

onAssisted.narration: The cook grabs the pole herself, and together you tip the pot slow and steady. The porridge pours out in one fat brown ribbon into a row of waiting bowls, and she wraps a hot supper in a cloth for you. "Better than the porridge at MILE 3," she says. "That is not hard." Down the road, a wagon is stuck right across the way.

interaction_planks.narration: The wagon is out, but the rut it leaves is deep as a bathtub, and a line of carts is already creeping up behind. "Planks!" cries the driver, pointing at a stack by the ditch. "Fill the rut before the next fellow sinks! Hand them down, hand them down!" So everyone lines up along the road, and the planks start to travel from hand to hand like a very slow train.

interaction.cue: Catch the plank, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: The last plank drops into the rut, flat and snug. The first cart behind rolls over it without a single bump, and the driver presses a few coins into your hand. "Plank money," he says gruffly. "I was admiring the view, but I am also grateful."

onFailure.narration: One plank goes in sideways and sticks up like a drawbridge. The first cart behind goes over it with a bump and a bang. The driver sighs, stamps it flat and says it will do. "It's a rut," he says. "It has had worse."

onAssisted.narration: The driver takes the middle of the line himself, and the planks fly down it, hand to hand to hand. The rut fills flat and snug, and he presses a few coins into your hand. "Plank money," he says gruffly. "I was admiring the view, but I am also grateful."

interaction_hum.narration: Before you step away, Old Lintel rumbles one more thing. "Hear the note first," he says. "Then you will know it when it comes around again." He hums it, low enough to rattle the pebbles: low, high, middle, low. "Now you," he says. "Hum it back."

interaction.cue: Listen to the note, then hum it back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: You hum it back, low, high, middle, low, and under your boots the bridge hums with you, very faintly. Old Lintel's mossy face does something that might be a smile. "There," he says. "You will know it again." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the queue camp.

onFailure.narration: You hum a pretty tune. It is not the note. The bridge hums back, low and flat, as if politely correcting you. Old Lintel hums it once more, slower, and you get close enough. "Close," he says. "Close counts, for a first time." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the queue camp.

onAssisted.narration: Old Lintel hums along underneath you to hold the note up, low, high, middle, low, and the bridge hums with you, very faintly. "There," he says. "You will know it again." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the queue camp.
